original_title: ADC Synthesis by Conjugation to Lysine Residues.
title: Back to basics: ADCs via plain lysine conjugation
blurb: The original ADC conjugation route, hanging payload off whatever lysines happen to sit on the surface. Simple and well-worn, but it's the method that gives you the heterogeneous DAR smear site-specific techniques exist to avoid.

original_title: An Integrated Introduction to Payload and Linker Design in ADC Development.
title: A primer on picking your ADC's payload and linker
blurb: An overview chapter walking through how payload and linker choices interact in ADC design, the kind of thing you read before committing to a chemistry, not after.

original_title: In Situ RP-HPLC Analysis of Intact Antibody-Drug Conjugates for Reaction Monitoring and DAR Trend Estimation.
title: Watching DAR climb in real time with RP-HPLC
blurb: A protocol for running intact ADCs on RP-HPLC during the conjugation reaction itself, tracking the DAR trend as it happens instead of guessing from an endpoint sample.

original_title: Preparing Site-Specific Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADC) Through Noncanonical Amino Acid Mutagenesis.
title: Site-specific ADCs by writing a new amino acid into the sequence
blurb: Site-specific conjugation via noncanonical amino acid mutagenesis, giving the payload a single defined handle that isn't a native cysteine or lysine. One more route around the native-residue conjugation mess.

original_title: Tag-Free Lipoic Acid Ligase A (LplA)-Mediated Modification Toward Antibody-Drug Conjugate Production.
title: Enzyme-tagging an ADC without the usual tag
blurb: Lipoic acid ligase normally needs a short peptide tag to find its site, this protocol claims tag-free site-specific labeling for ADC production instead. Keeps the enzymatic precision without engineering in extra sequence.

original_title: Antibody-Drug Conjugate (ADC) Characterization by Size Exclusion Chromatography Coupled with Mass Spectrometry.
title: Sizing up ADCs with SEC straight into MS
blurb: A protocol coupling size-exclusion chromatography directly to mass spec for ADC characterization, catching aggregate and species detail that either technique alone would miss.

original_title: Synthesis, crystal structure, Hirshfeld analysis and spectroscopic characterization of a norbornene- N -hydroxysuccinimide bifunctional linker
title: A norbornene-NHS ester linker gets its crystal structure solved
blurb: Diels-Alder chemistry followed by esterification builds a bifunctional linker with a norbornene on one end and an NHS ester on the other, and this paper is mostly about proving it: single-crystal structure in the monoclinic P21/n space group, plus a Hirshfeld surface analysis mapping the intermolecular contacts. Structural characterization of a reagent, not a use case.
venue: Acta Crystallographica Section E Crystallographic Communications

original_title: Dual-Drug ADC Synthesis Using a Combination of Nonnatural Amino Acid and Cysteine-Based Conjugations.
title: One antibody, two drugs, two different attachment chemistries
blurb: A methods chapter on building dual-drug ADCs by putting one payload on a cysteine and the other on a genetically encoded nonnatural amino acid, so each warhead's loading can be tuned independently. Protocol, not new data.

original_title: ITM and AtomVie Global Radiopharma Enter Supply Agreement for n.c.a. Lutetium-177 - Yahoo Finance
title: ITM locks up another Lutetium-177 supplier
blurb: ITM signs a supply deal with AtomVie for n.c.a. Lutetium-177. Pure capacity news, but Lu-177 supply has been the perennial bottleneck for radioligand therapy, so it matters who's actually feeding the pipeline.

original_title: Disulfide Crosslink Density is a Key Determinant in the Formation, Dynamics, and Maturation of Cysteine-rich Designer Biomolecular Condensates.
title: Disulfide density as the dial for how a condensate behaves
blurb: In cysteine-rich designer condensates, how densely you crosslink with disulfides, not just the sequence, controls how fast they form, how fluid they stay inside, and whether they eventually mature into something stiffer. A tuning knob for synthetic condensates.

original_title: The Architecture of Antibody-Drug Conjugates: Key Design Parameters and Methodological Approaches.
title: The ADC design knobs, laid out in one chapter
blurb: A reference rundown of what actually governs ADC performance: linker chemistry, conjugation site, drug-to-antibody ratio, and the assays used to pin them down. Useful as a checklist, not a result.

original_title: Radiolabeling of Monoclonal Antibodies with Zirconium-89 for Immuno-PET Imaging.
title: The Zr-89 antibody labeling recipe, step by step
blurb: A protocols chapter for conjugating and radiolabeling monoclonal antibodies with zirconium-89 for immuno-PET. If you're setting the chemistry up yourself, this is the how-to; otherwise there's nothing new to report here.

original_title: Affibody-conjugated hyaluronic acid hydrogels within collagen sponges enhance dose-dependent BMP-2-mediated bone formation and repair of critically sized femoral defects
title: Affibodies hidden in a collagen sponge tame BMP-2's burst release
blurb: BMP-2 dumped straight off a collagen sponge releases too fast, causing inflammation and bone growing where it shouldn't, and the usual fix of denser crosslinking stiffens the gel enough to keep cells out. This builds a hyaluronic acid hydrogel loaded with BMP-2-binding affibodies inside the same clinical sponge to hold the growth factor back without that tradeoff, and it produced dose-dependent bone repair in a critical-size femoral defect. The retention trick doesn't cost you actual healing.

original_title: NET-Inhibiting Bio-Orthogonal Gelated Neutrophils Reverse Maladaptive Trained Immunity and Protect Against Periodontitis Recurrence.
title: Gelled neutrophils that stop NETs from relearning bad habits
blurb: Periodontitis keeps recurring partly because neutrophils get locked into an overreactive trained-immunity state. This engineers neutrophils via bio-orthogonal gelation to block their NET release and reverse that trained memory, protecting against recurrence rather than just treating the flare. Thin on mechanism in what's available, but a genuinely different angle on the recurrence problem.

original_title: Chemical crosslinking enables profiling of endogenous cell surface galectin-3 interactions.
title: Fishing for galectin-3's real partners on the cell surface
blurb: A chemical crosslinking method to catch galectin-3's actual binding partners as they exist on live cell membranes, rather than whatever turns up in a lysate pulldown. A tool paper, but the kind that could settle what galectin-3 is actually doing out there.

original_title: Optimization of the proton-induced reaction <sup>155</sup>Gd(p,x)<sup>155</sup>Tb at energies between 7 and 26 MeV with highly-enriched <sup>155</sup>Gd targets
title: Dialing in the proton energy for making Terbium-155
blurb: Cross-section legwork for the Gd-155(p,x)Tb-155 reaction across 7-26 MeV using highly enriched Gd-155 targets, mapping which energy window actually gives clean Tb-155. Not flashy, but this is exactly the data production routes for the terbium theranostic family get built on.

original_title: Photoaffinity Capture of Unit-Resolved Ubiquitin–Decoder Contacts Underlying Topology-Selective Recognition of Heterotypic Chains
title: Catching which domain reads which ubiquitin in a mixed chain
blurb: Heterotypic K63/K48 polyubiquitin chains send different signals depending on how they're decoded, but nobody had a way to capture both the interaction and exactly where it happens on a chain of mixed linkage types. This uses diazirine-based photoaffinity capture to map unit-resolved contacts between decoder proteins and chain topology directly. A real methods advance for a question that's been stuck at 'we know topology matters' for a while.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Synthetic single-domain antibodies as immunoconjugate therapeutics.
title: Nanobodies get the immunoconjugate treatment
blurb: A review on building immunoconjugate drugs around single-domain antibodies instead of full-size ones. Smaller binder, presumably simpler payload chemistry, but it's a review summing up the field, not new data.

original_title: Degrader Antibody Conjugates: Design Considerations Toward DAC Synthesis.
title: What actually goes into a degrader-antibody conjugate
blurb: A methods chapter on the design choices behind degrader-antibody conjugates, which swap the usual cytotoxic payload for a targeted protein degrader delivered by the antibody. Protocol, not a new result.

original_title: Light-Mapping-Guided Photostability Assessment for Light-Sensitive Antibody-Drug Conjugates.
title: Mapping light exposure to see which ADCs can't take it
blurb: A protocol for assessing photostability in light-sensitive antibody-drug conjugates by mapping the light dose rather than guessing at bench lighting. The kind of thing you want to have run before your conjugate degrades in transit instead of in the paper.

original_title: “Click” formation of the imine bond in water
title: Imine clicking now works in water, even in cell lysate
blurb: Tuning the building blocks, rather than adding extra functional groups, gets imine bond formation to run cleanly in water and even inside cell lysate, with either aromatic or aliphatic amines. That's enough to do dynamic combinatorial chemistry at submillimolar concentrations in plain water, no special conditions required.

original_title: Unraveling Synergistic Substrate–H 2 Activation and Tunable Counteranion Effects in Ru‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogenation of 2‐Substituted Quinolines: An Integrated Kinetic and DFT Study
title: The rate-limiting step in quinoline hydrogenation isn't fixed, it moves
blurb: Kinetics plus DFT on Ru-catalyzed asymmetric hydrogenation of 2-substituted quinolines show both the quinoline itself and the dihydroquinoline intermediate acting as proton acceptors, so the rate-determining step actually shifts between the first and second H2 heterolytic cleavage depending on conditions, with the counteranion tuning which one wins. A mechanism paper, not a new catalyst.

original_title: Characterization of Antibody-Drug Conjugates Using Hydrophobic Interaction Chromatography Coupled with Mass Spectrometry.
title: Sizing up ADC drug loading with HIC-MS
blurb: A methods chapter on using hydrophobic interaction chromatography coupled to mass spec to characterize antibody-drug conjugates, presumably for sorting out drug-to-antibody ratios without denaturing the antibody. Protocol, not new chemistry.

original_title: Visible-Light-Induced Three-Component Minisci-Type Trifluoroalkylation of Electron-Deficient Heteroaromatics
title: Trifluoroalkylating electron-poor heterocycles with no catalyst anywhere
blurb: A three-component Minisci-type trifluoroalkylation that skips the metal, the photocatalyst, and the acid, running instead through a polarity-reversal cascade off trifluoromethyl thianthrenium triflate as the CF3 radical source. Aerobic and operationally simple, aimed right at the electron-poor heteroarenes pharma keeps wanting a CF3 group bolted onto.

original_title: Preparation of (124)I-Labeled Antibodies via Direct Electrophilic Substitution.
title: A direct route to iodine-124-labeled antibodies
blurb: A methods chapter on labeling antibodies with iodine-124 via direct electrophilic substitution, the kind of protocol you need before you can even think about PET imaging with the thing. No new chemistry claimed, just the recipe.

original_title: Harnessing regioselective aryl migration of pyridone-based aryl-λ3-iodonium salts to access iodine-substituted aryloxypyridines
title: Hook-and-slide iodonium chemistry lands iodine right where aryloxypyridines need it
blurb: Koser's reagent first builds a pyridonyl(aryl)iodonium salt with C3 selectivity, the hook, then an iodine-to-oxygen aryl migration slides the aryl group over with O selectivity. The payoff is access to iodine-substituted aryloxypyridine scaffolds, common in drugs but hard to make with multiple substituents, and it works because the new iodonium salts carry two nucleophilic sites sitting right next to each other.

original_title: Late-Stage Skeletal Editing of the Arylacetic Acid Pharmacophore: A Photocatalytic Route to Oxetan-3-ol Bioisosteres
title: Swap indomethacin's acid for an oxetanol and COX-1 backs off
blurb: A transition-metal-free photocatalytic decarboxylative coupling turns arylacetic acids straight into oxetan-3-ol bioisosteres, no organometallics needed, and it even handles electron-deficient acids and strained ketones. Lipophilicity jumps by up to 2.5 log units, which sounds like a problem, but on the indomethacin analogue it keeps COX-2 inhibition at 191 nM while dulling COX-1 to 280 nM, pushing the selectivity index from 0.20 to 1.47, a possible route to less GI toxicity off the same old scaffold.

original_title: Gold‐Catalyzed “Anti‐Baldwin” Cyclization of Unactivated Alkenes
title: Baldwin's rules bent, not broken
blurb: 5-endo-trig cyclizations are supposed to be a bad bet, kinetically, especially on unactivated alkenes. This gold catalysis gets there anyway by letting the favored 4-exo-trig pathway form reversibly, so the system equilibrates over to the disfavored 5-endo-trig intermediate and reacts from there. Thermodynamics doing an end-run around kinetics.

original_title: Aryl Palladium Acetates as Highly Active Species in Intermolecular Heck Reactions of Hindered Olefins
title: Heck reactions finally get past hindered olefins
blurb: Tri- and tetrasubstituted olefins have been a Heck-reaction blind spot since the 1970s, usually patched with directing groups or exotic cationic Pd species from triflates and diazonium salts. This one just uses plain PdCl2 or Pd(OAc)2 with aryl iodides and bromides, no directing group, and bills itself as the first general version that actually handles hindered alkenes.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Multigram Synthesis of the 1,3-Substituted Cuneane Amino Acids
title: Cuneane amino acids, now on the gram scale
blurb: Cuneanes mimic the exit vectors of meta- and para-substituted benzenes and come from cubanes in one step, but there was no usable amino acid building block made from them until now. A Curtius rearrangement on cuneane halfesters gets both 1,3-regioisomers as Boc amino esters in 84-91% yield at 10 g scale, then on to the standard Boc/Fmoc acids and esters. Unglamorous, but it's the building-block paper that quietly unblocks everyone else's work.

original_title: Bovine Serum Albumin-Crosslinked Silk Fibroin-Based Bioink via Thiol-Ene Click Chemistry for Bone Tissue Engineering.
title: A silk bioink clicked together for bone scaffolds
blurb: Silk fibroin crosslinked with bovine serum albumin via thiol-ene click chemistry, pitched as a bioink for bone tissue engineering. No performance numbers to go on, just the formulation.

original_title: Heparin-Decorated Hydrogel Microspheres Enable Bioactive Islet Encapsulation and Sustained Glycemic Control in Diabetic Mice.
title: Heparin-coated microspheres to keep transplanted islets working
blurb: Islet cells get wrapped in heparin-decorated hydrogel microspheres, which stayed bioactive and kept blood sugar under control in diabetic mice. Mouse data, so it's a step toward encapsulated islet transplants rather than one yet.

original_title: An Organocatalytic Borrowing Hydrogen Reaction by Flavin Photocatalyst
title: A flavin photocatalyst runs the full borrowing-hydrogen cycle without a metal
blurb: Borrowing hydrogen chemistry is normally a transition-metal game built on polar, two-electron hydride transfer, ligands and heat included. Swapping in a flavin photocatalyst gets the whole cycle running organocatalytically instead, on what the authors say is a genuine mechanistic switch away from that usual hydride route. Cheaper and milder if the substrate scope backs it up.

original_title: Rh(III)-Catalyzed Regiodivergent Enantioselective C2- and C4–H Alkylation of Indoles
title: One Rh catalyst, two different spots on the indole, your choice
blurb: Rh(III) catalysis lets you dial C2- or C4-selective alkylation of indoles with nitroalkenes just by tuning reaction parameters, no second catalyst needed, and still pulls up to 97% yield, 96% ee, and >10:1 regioselectivity. The switchable regiodivergence is the actual trick here, not the alkylation itself.

original_title: Spontaneous Intermolecular Cross‐Linking Produces Aβ Dimers With Multiple Alzheimer's Disease Relevant Activities
title: Aβ dimers form on their own, and they're the same ones found in plaques
blurb: Covalently cross-linked Aβ1-42 dimers show up spontaneously just from incubating Aβ fibrils long enough, carrying the same Asp1-Glu22 and Asp1-Asp1 isopeptide bonds seen in disease-relevant higher-order aggregates. That implies the toxic dimers can form after the fibrils do rather than needing to seed them, which had been an open question.

original_title: Gram-Scale Synthesis of the Opiate Alkaloids Mitragynine and Speciociliatine
title: Mitragynine made by the gram, from scratch
blurb: A 13-step enantioselective, convergent route from 4-methoxyindole and 1,3-propanediol reaches mitragynine, the main active alkaloid in kratom, at 15% overall yield but gram-scale, along with its relative speciociliatine. The payoff is a reliable synthetic source for these μ-opioid-active alkaloids instead of depending on plant extraction.

original_title: Copper-Catalyzed Atroposelective Hydroaminocarbonylation of Alkynes: Access to Axially Chiral Amides
title: Axially chiral amides out of alkynes, copper doing the twisting
blurb: Open-chain axially chiral styrenes are notoriously hard to lock down because they rotate too freely to hold a stable axis. A copper hydride catalyst with CO and O-benzoyl hydroxylamines does atroposelective hydroaminocarbonylation on internal alkynes to get there anyway, landing decent regio- and enantioselectivity under mild conditions.

original_title: Protecting-group-lean platform for synthesizing diverse phenylethanoid glycosides uncovers antifibrotic leads
title: A leaner route to phenylethanoid glycosides turns up antifibrotic hits
blurb: Phenylethanoid glycosides are all over traditional medicine but a pain to make in variety, so nobody's really nailed their structure-activity relationships. This platform cuts the protecting-group busywork and builds a 29-member library by varying four spots on the central glucose, and some of those analogs come out as antifibrotic leads. The library is the real payoff here, the leads still need following up.

original_title: PEG-free tunable poly(2-oxazoline) lipids modulate mRNA-LNP biodistribution and expression in vivo
title: PEG-free lipids for mRNA delivery, and you can dial them
blurb: Poly(2-oxazoline) lipids stand in for the usual PEG shell on mRNA-LNPs, and tuning the polymer changes where the particles end up in the body and how much protein they make. Ducking PEG also ducks the anti-PEG antibody problem that keeps nagging these formulations, assuming it holds up beyond this result.

original_title: Directing Cell Fate via Spatiotemporally Patterned Viscoelasticity Driven by Dynamic Crosslink Exchange.
title: Patterning a gel's squishiness in space and time to steer cell fate
blurb: Dynamic crosslink exchange lets them pattern a hydrogel's viscoelasticity across both space and time, and that pattern alone is enough to push cells toward different fates. Still a preprint, so the fate-steering claim hasn't been through review yet.

original_title: Synergistic Lewis Base Organocatalysis and Electrocatalysis for the Enantioselective Construction of α‐Fluorinated Quaternary Stereocenters
title: Electrochemistry teams up with isothiourea catalysis for fluorinated quaternary centers
blurb: α-fluorinated quaternary stereocenters are exactly the motif pharma wants and exactly the one nobody enjoys making enantioselectively. Here anodic single-electron oxidation pairs with a chiral isothiourea catalyst to alkylate bench-stable fluorinated acetic esters with silyl enol ethers and allylsilanes, highly enantioselectively. Nice that the fluorinated starting esters are shelf-stable instead of something you babysit.

original_title: N ‐Heterocyclic Carbene/Nickel‐Catalyzed Enantioselective Alkylation of Aldehydes With Secondary Trialkylboron Reagents
title: Turning aldehydes into chiral secondary alcohols with boron nucleophiles
blurb: A nickel/NHC catalyst alkylates aldehydes using secondary alkylboron reagents as the nucleophile, giving chiral secondary alcohols in high yield and ee. The trick is a bulky C2-symmetric NHC ligand doing the steering, which matters because secondary boron nucleophiles are usually the sluggish, unselective ones.

original_title: Cascade Synthesis of Alternating Thiolactone–Episulfide Copolymers via Multi-Site Single-Unit Monomer Insertion
title: Getting thiolactones and episulfides to alternate instead of homopolymerizing
blurb: Thiolactones and episulfides are cheap, biobased sulfur heterocycles, but left to their own devices they'd rather homopolymerize than alternate. This two-step cascade builds the alternation in first and polymerizes second, sidestepping the cross-propagation problem that's blocked this combination until now.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Programmable Amino Migration−Enabled Diversification of Allylamines
title: Making allylamines do more than just sit there as alkenes
blurb: Radical migration chemistry on alkenes usually funnels the translocated intermediate into one fixed reaction path. This platform redirects allylamines' migrating radicals into several different manifolds instead, turning what used to be a passive alkene substrate into a jumping-off point for divergent synthesis.

original_title: From a Dinitrogen‐Derived Hydrazido Complex to Inorganic Ammonium‐Type Cores Through Aluminum‐Promoted N─N Bond Cleavage
title: Splitting N-N bonds to build ammonium cores instead of the usual nitrides
blurb: Cleaving the N-N bond in dinitrogen-derived complexes almost always hands you nitride fragments. Treating a chromium bis(silyl)hydrazido complex with AlMe3 instead splits the bond homolytically and assembles two inorganic ammonium-type cores in a single CrN2Al2Si2 unit, each central nitrogen bonded to chromium, two aluminums, and a silicon. DFT backs a pathway where AlMe3 strips the N-substituent first. Fundamental dinitrogen chemistry, not anything headed for a reactor soon.

original_title: Ester-Directed Reductive Kinetic Resolution of Alkyl-Alkyl Sulfoxides by (Salen)Titanium Catalysis
title: Resolving alkyl-alkyl sulfoxides by reducing away the enantiomer you don't want
blurb: Chiral alkyl-alkyl sulfoxides are hard to get at by reduction, so this kinetic resolution hangs a pendant ester off the sulfoxide to chelate a chiral (salen)titanium catalyst, which then deoxygenates one enantiomer preferentially. Recovered sulfoxide reaches up to 96% ee, though s values topping out around 12 mean it won't work equally well on everything.

original_title: Iron‐Catalyzed Tandem Benzylic Oxidation/Betti Reaction: Direct Synthesis of Betti’s Bases From Methylarenes
title: Turning plain methylarenes straight into Betti's bases, no aldehyde needed
blurb: Betti bases normally start from an aldehyde, but cheap FeCl3 plus TBHP oxidizes methylarenes to the aldehyde in situ and rolls straight into the three-component reaction with β-naphthol and an aminoheterocycle, all in one pot, good to excellent yields. Saves having to source or make the aldehyde separately.

original_title: Regioselective [3+3] Annulation of Morita–Baylis–Hillman Carbonates with In Situ-Generated Thioureas: A Modular Approach to Iminothiazinones
title: Building iminothiazinones by making the thiourea on the fly
blurb: Lewis base catalysis strings an amine, an isothiocyanate, and a Morita-Baylis-Hillman carbonate together into a thiourea that then S-allylates and cyclizes itself into 2-imino-1,3-thiazinones. Unsymmetric thioureas pick the more nucleophilic nitrogen every single time, and it scales to grams without issue.

original_title: Visible-Light Photoredox-Catalyzed Cascade Fluoroalkylation/Cyclization of N -Methacryloyl Hydrazones with RfSO2Na for the Synthesis of Rf-Substituted Pyrazolones
title: Photoredox builds fluoroalkylated pyrazolones straight from hydrazones
blurb: Visible light kicks off a radical cascade with sodium fluoroalkanesulfinates, tacking a fluoroalkyl group onto N-methacryloyl hydrazones and cyclizing them into pyrazolones in one pot. Works across aryl, heteroaryl, and aliphatic aldehyde-derived hydrazones under mild conditions, so it's mostly a drop-in for the usual Rf-radical chemistry.

original_title: Merck’s TROP2 ADC extends survival in pivotal gastroesophageal cancer trial
title: Merck's TROP2 ADC notches its second phase 3 survival win
blurb: Sacituzumab tirumotecan improved overall survival in a pivotal phase 3 gastroesophageal cancer trial, Merck's second global phase 3 win for this TROP2 ADC. No numbers disclosed yet, but beating on survival twice is a real result, not just a response-rate headline.

original_title: Machine Learning-Enhanced ATR-FTIR Spectroscopy for Rapid, Low-Cost Glycan Quantification
title: Swapping the glycan assay for FTIR and a regression model
blurb: Antibody glycosylation is a critical quality attribute, but testing for it normally means slow, expensive separations. This pairs ATR-FTIR spectra with a machine-learning regression to estimate N-glycan levels instead, cheap and fast if the calibration holds up across batches.

original_title: Metal Fluorides as Heterogeneous Base Catalysts: Exceptional C-C Bond Formation Activity from LaF 3
title: A fluoride surface that out-bases hydrotalcite
blurb: A screen of rare-earth and alkaline-earth fluorides found LaF3 matching or beating Mg-Al hydrotalcite, the usual go-to, at catalyzing C-C bond formation. Hammett plots and kinetic isotope effects point to basic sites activating the nitroalkane as the actual mechanism, not just surface area.

original_title: Development of a phenyl-bridged bis-β-carboline-crosslinked hyaluronic acid polymer: synergistic eradication of drug-resistant Gram-positive bacteria
title: A biofilm-busting hydrogel that releases its payload on cue
blurb: Hyaluronic acid crosslinked with a phenyl-bridged bis-beta-carboline only breaks down when hyaluronidase shows up, which is convenient since that's what resistant biofilms secrete. It boosts ciprofloxacin against drug-resistant Gram-positive bacteria, limits resistance from developing, and helps wounds heal.

original_title: Total Synthesis of the Saponin Vaccine Adjuvant Chiococcasaponin I via a Sequential One-Pot Tetrasaccharide Assembly
title: Thirteen steps from a cheap triterpenoid to a vaccine adjuvant saponin
blurb: First total synthesis of chiococcasaponin I, and the hard part is its branched tetrasaccharide, two beta-D-apiofuranoses plus a rhamnose-arabinose core. They forge all three glycosidic bonds in one pot instead of stepwise, with the whole convergent route running 13 steps from commercial oleanolic acid.

original_title: Synthesis of the Epimer of the Cytotoxic Prenylated 2,3‐Dihydrobenzofuran‐3‐ol Isolated From Atractylodes lancea (Thunb.) DC and Dehydro‐Oberoniamyosurusin I From a Common Precursor
title: Two natural products, one precursor, and a stereochemistry fix that didn't work
blurb: Starting from methylparaben, an organocatalytic intramolecular aldol builds the dihydrobenzofuran core, then an O-allylation/Claisen rearrangement and a Grubbs II cross metathesis install the prenyl chain, delivering both the epimer of a cytotoxic Atractylodes lancea metabolite and dehydro-oberoniamyosurusin I. Trying to invert the benzylic alcohol's stereochemistry just dehydrated it instead, so the epimer is apparently what you're stuck with.

original_title: AAV peptide-conjugated LNPs highlight bottlenecks in LNP-mRNA delivery to photoreceptors.
title: LNPs still can't quite reach photoreceptors
blurb: Conjugating AAV-derived peptides onto lipid nanoparticles was the attempt at getting mRNA into photoreceptors, and the result mostly maps out where that delivery route still bottlenecks. A reminder that retinal gene delivery isn't solved just by swapping AAV for LNPs.

original_title: Amorphous intermediates direct polymorph selection in the crystallization of 3-chloromandelic acid
title: The least stable polymorph wins first, every time
blurb: Racemic 3-chloromandelic acid has three polymorphs stable at room temperature, and crystal structure prediction would bet on the thermodynamically favored one. Instead the least stable form, RS3, forms reproducibly across multiple solvents whenever supersaturation is high, then converts to the more stable forms later via solvent-mediated and heat-induced transitions. Kinetics beating thermodynamics again, this time apparently routed through an amorphous intermediate.

original_title: Bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes as saturated bioisosteres of meta-benzene
title: Swap in a bicyclohexane, keep the drug working
blurb: Back in 2019 they guessed bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes could stand in for meta-substituted benzene rings. Now they've shown it in two real drugs: swap it into sonidegib and the physicochemical properties and membrane permeability hold up, swap it into meclizine and metabolic stability actually improves while the anticancer activity stays put.

original_title: The Dialkylphosphinoyl Motif: Synthetic Access and Applications in Medicinal Chemistry
title: Phosphine oxides stop being the unwanted byproduct
blurb: A review on how the dimethylphosphinoyl group in brigatinib, the first FDA-approved anticancer drug with a phosphine oxide in it, turned a reaction byproduct chemists used to throw away into something worth designing around, and rounds up how people are now making dialkylphosphinoyl fragments on purpose.

original_title: LMCT-Enabled Ferrioxalate Reductive C–O Bond Cleavage of Activated Aldehydes and Ketones
title: Iron photocatalysis strips C-O bonds without a precious metal
blurb: Shine light on ferrioxalate and you get a ligand-to-metal charge transfer that spits out a strongly reducing Fe(I), which tears the C-O bond off activated aldehydes and ketones and swaps it for cyanide. Works across a broad range of aliphatic and aromatic substrates, and it does it with iron instead of whatever precious metal usually gets the job.

original_title: Catalytic Aziridination With Simple Acyl Azides via Validated Copper‐Acyl Nitrenes
title: Copper-acyl nitrenes, actually caught this time
blurb: People have been invoking copper nitrenes as the reactive intermediate in N-group transfer for years without ever pinning one down. Here simple aryl acyl azides generate ten copper-acyl nitrenes that get nailed by NMR, EPR, and computation, singlet ground state and all, and the things still convert styrene to N-acyl aziridines in up to 76% yield.

original_title: Dearomatization and cycloaddition of furans and indoles enable divergent syntheses of spirooxindole alkaloids
title: Dearomatize two heterocycles, then crash them together
blurb: A green oxidative dearomatization of indoles and furans, then a formal cycloaddition between the two dearomatized halves, built to reach spirooxindole alkaloids that divergent synthesis usually struggles with.

original_title: Black Titanium‐Oxo Cluster as a Dual‐Mode Catalyst for Regioselective Protein Editing
title: A titanium-oxo cluster stable enough to edit a protein
blurb: These clusters are usually too fragile in water to be useful for anything biological. This hexanuclear one holds together long enough to act as a light-driven, dual-mode catalyst for regioselective editing on β-lactoglobulin, helped along by an unusually low 1.56 eV optical gap for a TiO2 analogue.

original_title: Rational Ligand Design to Enforce the fac-fac Coordination Geometry
title: A ligand that won't let the metal isomerize on you
blurb: The PQPD scaffold locks a metal center into fac-fac coordination instead of letting it drift between isomers. Aimed squarely at the thermal stability olefin polymerization catalysts need to keep performing in an actual industrial process, not just in the glovebox.

original_title: Mechanistic Origin of Base and Solvent Effects in Triazene Formation from Arylazo Sulfones: Cooperative Roles of Na+, HCO3–, and MeOH
title: Why NaHCO3 in methanol, specifically, makes triazene synthesis work
blurb: Arylazo sulfones only give high triazene yields with NaHCO3 in MeOH, and nobody really knew why. DFT plus control experiments say the sulfone binds an NaHCO3 dimer before N-S cleavage kicks off a diazonium-sulfinate ion pair that the amine then adds into, with Na+, bicarbonate, and methanol all cooperating rather than one of them just being along for the ride.

original_title: A Room‐Temperature Fluorescent‐Free Imidazol‐2‐Ylidene: A Versatile Platform for Fluorophore Diversification
title: A free NHC that actually glows at room temperature
blurb: Free N-heterocyclic carbenes are normally photophysically dead. Bolt a tetrahedral boron into the backbone of the classic IMes carbene and you get the first isolable free imidazol-2-ylidene that fluoresces in both solution and solid state, with calculations showing the carbene carbon itself sits in the lowest excited state rather than just watching from the sidelines.

original_title: Valency-Driven Library Design Enables Single-Round Evolution of Circular Aptamers with Programmable Binding Affinities
title: How many binding sites per aptamer actually matters
blurb: Dial up the valency of a circular DNA library, one, two, or three randomized motifs per construct, and run a single round of selection against two model proteins: monovalent libraries land moderate-affinity binders, and more copies per construct buy tighter, more specific aptamers without needing the usual multi-round selection grind.

original_title: PCET beyond p K a : Disaggregation and Additional Base Effects as Neglected Key Factors for Unlocking Inaccessible Substrates in Direct Intermolecular Photocatalytic Ring‐Opening Remote Alkylation of Cycloalkanols
title: Swap the base, not the arene, to reach harder cycloalkanols
blurb: MS-PCET ring-opening alkylation of cycloalkanols has mostly worked only on substrates dressed up with electron-rich arenes like PMP, because that's what made the O-H bond abstractable. This paper says the real lever was never just the base's pKa but disaggregation effects from the base partner, and tuning that opens up nonactivated substrates that were previously stuck on the bench.

original_title: Towards next generation enzyme mimics through local electric field control in organic cage catalysts
title: How much of an enzyme's speed is just a well-aimed electric field
blurb: Organic cage catalysts built to mimic enzymes find that about half the field interaction energy actually converts into catalysis, good for a projected two-orders-of-magnitude rate boost. But it only works if you lock down both the reactant complex and the transition state in the field, which hints at why real enzymes bind so tightly: not just to hold the substrate still, but to hold it strained in exactly the right field.

original_title: Transducing a CO2 Concentration Gradient into Electrical Energy through Copper–Ethylenediamine Coordination
title: Turning a CO2 gradient directly into a voltage
blurb: Ethylenediamine binds Cu2+ and keeps it dissolved, but CO2 protonates the amine and kills that coordination, pushing the system toward metallic Cu instead. Rig two Cu electrodes with a Cu-ethylenediamine electrolyte across a CO2 concentration difference and you get an open-circuit voltage out of what's otherwise just a gas gradient quietly equilibrating.

original_title: A Cryptic Cytochrome P450 Radical Cyclase Catalyzes Naphthalene-Ring Closure in Rifamycin Biosynthesis
title: The enzyme that beats rifamycin's chromophore to the wrong answer
blurb: Left alone in solution, the rifamycin precursor prorifamycin A spontaneously collapses into a dead-end deoxynaphthoquinone. A cryptic P450, Rif-Orf0, acts as a radical cyclase that grabs it first, closing the naphthalene ring correctly into the 8-hydroxy intermediate before the nonenzymatic decay pathway can ruin it. A nice case of an enzyme existing specifically to outrun its own substrate's instability.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Brentuximab Vedotin With or Without Nivolumab in Treating Patients With Relapsed or Refractory CD30+ Lymphoma
title: Adding nivolumab to brentuximab vedotin for CD30+ lymphoma relapse
blurb: A Phase 2 trial testing brentuximab vedotin alone against brentuximab vedotin plus nivolumab in relapsed or refractory CD30+ Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma. University of Washington is running it, and it's already closed to new recruitment.

original_title: Crystal Structure of the Chiral Iron(II) Δ-[FeCl{(R,R)-Me-Duphos(O)2}2](BF4)·CH2Cl2 Compound
title: A chiral iron catalyst candidate, caught on camera
blurb: Crystal structure of a chiral Fe(II) complex with Me-Duphos(O)2 ligands, made by O2 oxidizing the parent FeH2 compound. The pitch for iron oxophosphines is the usual one: iron's cheap and abundant, the ligands are air-stable, and that combination is attractive for enantioselective catalysis. This is just the structure, though, no catalytic numbers yet.

original_title: Electropositive Site Engineering via Ordered Intermetallic Electrocatalysts for Hydrogen Evolution: From M 2P to Zr2 M 12P7 ( M = Ni, Co, Fe)
title: Ordering the P-M sites instead of just doping them
blurb: Doped and alloyed transition metal phosphide HER catalysts give you a messy spread of local structures that makes structure-property relationships hard to pin down. Ordered ternary Zr2M12P7 phases (M = Ni, Co, Fe) give each element its own distinct crystallographic site instead, so cranking up the second metal's electropositive character becomes an actual tunable knob rather than something averaged out by disorder.

original_title: Can we trust a positive PSMA PET/CT before the Phoenix threshold? Positive predictive value after primary radiotherapy for prostate cancer. A retrospective cohort study
title: A positive PSMA PET before the Phoenix call might not mean much
blurb: A retrospective cohort looking at how reliable a positive PSMA PET/CT really is when it shows up before a patient has even hit the Phoenix biochemical-recurrence threshold after primary radiotherapy. Basically a positive predictive value check on whether that early scan is worth acting on.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Entropic Self-Standing Aluminosilicate Monoliths with Hierarchical Porosity and Their Catalytic Efficiencies: MUB-121( x ) Series
title: When your monolith's aluminum doesn't all show up to work
blurb: MUB-121(x) aluminosilicate monoliths, grown self-standing with hierarchical macro- and mesoporosity via a dodecane-in-water emulsion template and calcined at 700°C, come out with evenly distributed Al by elemental mapping. But not all of that Al actually lands in catalytically useful framework sites, which is exactly the kind of gap NMR and pyridine-probe FTIR exist to catch.

original_title: O 2 -tolerant CO 2 -to-CO reduction by air-sensitive carbon monoxide dehydrogenases in hydrated deep eutectic solvents
title: Shielding an oxygen-allergic enzyme well enough to run it in air
blurb: Carbon monoxide dehydrogenase normally dies the moment it meets O2, but parking it on functionalized carbon nanotubes inside a hydrated deep eutectic solvent lets it keep doing CO2-to-CO bioelectrocatalysis under aerobic conditions. A protective matrix doing the job an anaerobic glovebox usually has to.

original_title: Front Cover: High Fatigue‐Resistant Photoswitches Based on iridium(III)‐DTE Systems
title: A photoswitch that doesn't get tired
blurb: An iridium(III)-dithienylethene photoswitch built specifically to resist the fatigue that kills most molecular switches after repeated cycling, apparently sturdy enough to land the journal's front cover.

original_title: Unlocking catalytic asymmetric transformations of sulfilimidoyl fluorides toward chiral sulfinimidate esters
title: Making sulfilimidoyl fluorides turn chiral
blurb: An asymmetric catalytic route converts sulfilimidoyl fluoride intermediates into chiral sulfinimidate esters, opening up sulfur stereocenters for drug discovery. The payoff: one chiral analog (3bg) beats its own racemic version on anti-inflammatory activity, which is exactly the kind of result that justifies bothering with the chiral synthesis at all.

original_title: Synthesis of Cellulose Nanofiber Hydrogel Beads from Typha angustifolia for the Immobilization of Protease
title: Turning an invasive cattail into an enzyme scaffold
blurb: Typha angustifolia, the cattail that wrecks wetland and irrigation management, gets its cellulose pulled out, oxidized, blended with PVA and crosslinked into nanofiber hydrogel beads that work as a support for immobilizing protease. A waste-to-value story more than a new enzyme-carrier breakthrough.

original_title: Cyclopropenimine Ligands: Coordination Chemistry and Catalytic Applications
title: What cyclopropenimines actually do once they're on a metal
blurb: A perspective on cyclopropenimine ligands, strong neutral nitrogen donors whose aromatic cyclopropenium backbone lets them go beyond ordinary dative bonding, including some structurally confirmed four-electron donation to metal centers. Mostly a stock-take of what's been characterized so far, not a new reaction.

original_title: Overall Survival With [(177)Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 in Chemotherapy-Naïve Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer: Bayesian Reanalysis of the PSMAfore Trial.
title: Does Lu-177-PSMA-617 actually move survival before chemo?
blurb: A Bayesian reanalysis of the PSMAfore trial's overall survival data in chemotherapy-naive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. It's squeezing a different read out of existing trial numbers rather than running a new trial, so weight it accordingly.

original_title: Transfer through chlorine
title: Catalysis that passes the baton through chlorine
blurb: A Nature Catalysis paper on a transfer reaction where chlorine itself acts as the intermediate carrying the group along, rather than a direct hand-off.

original_title: Radiopharmaceutical therapy in cancer: clinical momentum, biological complexity, and the next era of precision systemic radiation oncology.
title: Radiopharma therapy's next act
blurb: A review making the case that radiopharmaceutical therapy now has real clinical momentum, but the biology underneath it, dosimetry, resistance, combinations, is getting more complicated as it scales up into a bigger piece of precision oncology. Field-state summary, not new data.

original_title: Natural Products-Based Nitroxide Conjugates: Synthetic Strategies and Applications in Redox Medicine
title: Nitroxide spin labels, now grafted onto natural products
blurb: A review rounding up the ways people have bolted nitroxyl radical tags onto natural product scaffolds, with the spin label apparently able to boost activity, cut toxicity, and sharpen selective cytotoxicity. There's exactly one earlier review on this topic, so this is mostly a tidy inventory rather than new chemistry.

original_title: Amino Crosslinkers Market Forecast to 2035: ADC Development and Bioconjugation Demand Drive Expansion - IndexBox
title: Someone's forecasting the amino crosslinker market out to 2035
blurb: An industry report pinning ADC development and bioconjugation demand as the growth engine for amino crosslinkers through 2035. Market-research boilerplate, not a result from anyone's bench.

original_title: Expanding the methionine toolkit: L-cyanohomoalanine as a multifunctional analog
title: A cyanide-bearing methionine stand-in that E. coli just accepts
blurb: L-cyanohomoalanine gets loaded by E. coli's own methionyl-tRNA synthetase into sfGFP in methionine-starved cultures, same as feeding the bugs real methionine, no genetic code expansion needed. Useful specifically because it's a native-machinery swap, which means global incorporation across the whole proteome rather than one engineered site.

original_title: Experimental antibody-drug conjugate shows promising initial activity in head and neck cancers - Medical Xpress
title: Another ADC, this one going after head and neck cancer
blurb: An experimental antibody-drug conjugate reportedly shows promising early activity in head and neck cancers. That's an early-stage read, so the real numbers are still to come.

original_title: Phase I Trial of Novel Antibody-Drug Conjugate Shows Early Efficacy in Sarcoma - Bioengineer.org
title: Phase I sarcoma ADC posts early efficacy
blurb: A new antibody-drug conjugate shows early signs of activity in sarcoma in its Phase I trial. Sarcoma is a brutal place to read efficacy signals this early, so hold the enthusiasm until later-stage data shows up.

original_title: 1,2,3-Triazole derivatives enable therapeutic and diagnostic strategies for neurodegenerative diseases
title: Click chemistry triazoles take a swing at neurodegeneration
blurb: A review on 1,2,3-triazole hybrids made via copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne click chemistry, aimed at both treating and imaging diseases like Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and MS. The triazole's real job here is just being a stable linker between two active pieces, which is click chemistry's oldest trick dressed up as a disease strategy.

original_title: New Antibody-Drug Conjugate Improves Endometrial Cancer Survival - Cancer Health
title: An ADC claims a survival win in endometrial cancer
blurb: A newer antibody-drug conjugate reportedly improves survival in endometrial cancer. Good if it holds up, but the headline is the survival claim, not the actual numbers behind it.

original_title: Hydroxamate Reticular Chemistry beyond Metals: Single-Crystalline Two- and Three-Dimensional Boron–Hydroxamate Covalent Organic Frameworks
title: Hydroxamate reticular chemistry, minus the metal
blurb: Hydroxamate chelation usually builds metal-organic frameworks, but here it's wrangling boron instead, producing four single-crystal boron-hydroxamate COFs (SUM-306 through 309) spanning 2D honeycomb and 3D pcu-h nets. They needed Bayesian optimization just to grow a crystal big enough to solve by diffraction, which says plenty about how fiddly this chemistry still is.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: AtomVie Global Radiopharma and ITM Enter Supply Agreement for n.c.a. Lutetium-177 - Yahoo Finance
title: AtomVie and ITM lock down a no-carrier-added Lutetium-177 supply deal
blurb: A supply agreement between two radiopharma players for n.c.a. Lu-177, the isotope underpinning the current crop of radioligand therapies. Pure business plumbing, but plumbing that matters when the whole field keeps bumping into isotope supply limits.

original_title: £1.54 million funding to advance automated radiopharmaceutical production in the UK - Laboratory Talk
title: UK puts £1.54 million behind automating radiopharmaceutical production
blurb: New funding aimed at automating how radiopharmaceuticals get manufactured in the UK. Light on which production step actually gets the robots, but the money's real.

original_title: Ferrous Ion-Activatable Thiol-Selective Covalent-Reversible Electrophiles to Enhance Erastin-Induced Ferroptosis
title: A ferroptosis trigger that stays dormant until iron flips it on
blurb: An electrophile caged with an endoperoxide that ignores GSH and other biothiols until a ferrous ion cracks it open, unmasking the reactive Michael acceptor on site. Paired with erastin it pushes ferroptosis harder, and the whole point is dodging the GSH quenching that normally rescues cells from it.

original_title: Biomimetic N ‐Terminal Homologation of Amino Acids
title: Making β2-amino acids the way chemists already make β3 ones
blurb: β3-amino acid homologation via decarboxylation is well worn; the β2 side has been neglected. This uses photoredox catalysis and a radical translocation cascade to homologate amino acids at the N-terminus instead, filling in the homologue everyone kept skipping.

original_title: Operator-induced reduction of air kerma during backpack-based gamma-ray measurement
title: Holding the gamma backpack right cuts your own dose
blurb: A look at how the operator's own handling, not the detector itself, swings the air kerma picked up during backpack-based gamma-ray surveys. Dosimetry housekeeping for the person carrying the gear, not new instrumentation.

original_title: Large-Scale Synthesis of Diphenyliodonium Triflate in Green Solvent
title: Diphenyliodonium triflate without the dichloromethane
blurb: Swaps DCM, the usual solvent for making this workhorse iodine(III) phenylating reagent, for ethyl acetate, scales up fine, and skips the inert atmosphere while still posting a low E factor and a thermally stable product. Mostly a process-chemistry cleanup, but a useful one if you make this reagent a lot.

original_title: Catalytic Asymmetric Ring Contraction to Construct Chiral Tertiary Boronic Esters with Non-Adjacent Tertiary Stereocenters
title: One iridium catalyst, two stereocenters that aren't even next to each other
blurb: An Ir-catalyzed migratory coupling between in-situ cyclic boronates and allylic carbonates ring-contracts its way to chiral tertiary boronic esters carrying 1,3-non-adjacent tertiary stereocenters. The trick is a single chiral catalyst setting both the enantio- and diastereoselectivity, since spatially separated stereocenters are usually where these systems fall apart.

original_title: Catalytic Enantioselective Synthesis of Vinyl‐ and Fluoroalkyl‐Substituted Cyclopropanes and Cyclopropenes †
title: Bench-stable diazo stand-ins for vinyl and fluoroalkyl cyclopropanes
blurb: Vinyl triftosylhydrazones sub in as safe, shelf-stable diazo surrogates for a dirhodium-catalyzed [2+1] cycloaddition, generating the vinylfluoroalkyl carbene in situ. Works across aryl and alkyl alkenes plus terminal alkynes to give enantioenriched cyclopropanes and cyclopropenes, so the appeal is losing the usual diazo handling risk without losing scope.
